items.evidence: The function just calls itself over and over
items.note: The student correctly explains that a function calls itself.

items.evidence: a base case is optional if you know the recursive call will terminate on its own eventually
items.note: The student states that a base case is optional, which is a known misconception.
The student does not mention how a base case returns a result without further calls.
The student fails to explain that recursive calls must operate on a strictly smaller subproblem.
The student makes no mention of stack frames or the call stack.
The student does not address stack overflow errors caused by missing base cases.
The student does not mention iterative rewrites.
The student does not discuss tail call optimization.

target_reason: The student holds a misconception that the base case is optional.
target_focus: why the function needs a base case to stop
